canonical_definition: Instance Segmentation is the behavior of processing natural language instructions to generate pixel-level segmentations of specific objects or regions in images or videos, often requiring implicit or explicit reasoning to address complex queries beyond basic detection. It reflects capabilities in vision-language understanding, hallucination mitigation, and task-specific accuracy, commonly evaluated via metrics like gIoU/cIoU or COCO APmask in both benchmark and real-world scenarios. The task integrates language-guided reasoning with pixel-level precision, enabling models to execute segmentation actions across diverse contexts such as object selection, scene understanding, or geological survey.
